newsitem.title: UK: GA H1 TO PRODUCE HEALTHY PROFITS GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: GA H1 TO PRODUCE HEALTHY PROFITS GROWTH.

text.p: General Accident, the last of Britain's big composite insurers to publish interim results, is expected to post a healthy increase in profits when it reports next Tuesday.

Despite widespread evidence that the rating environment remains difficult, especially in the UK, the non-life performance is again likely to be helped by the portfolio's focus on short-tailed personal and small commercial risks.
Salomon Brothers are forecasting a small underwriting profit across the UK book in the second quarter despite margin erosion from prior years' price softening.
Analyst forecasts range from 218 to 266 million pounds ($423.1 million) with the majority above the 246 million pound level and a dividend of around 12.5 pence per share.
Last year the group produced operating profits of 194 million pounds.
A sharp fall in weather-related losses lifted GA to a record first quarter with operating profits doubling to 114 million pounds from 55 million pounds last year, beating analyst expectations.
Despite soft markets, the first quarter produced a UK underwriting profit with a strong performance in property and special niche classes offsetting motor.
Net asset value fell short of expectations in the first three months of the year, however, reflecting the company's policy of switching out of equities and into bonds.
The rapidly expanding life insurance and pensions arm increased profits by 45 percent in the first quarter following last year's acquisition of Provident Mutual.

Life profits are becoming an increasingly important component of the group's earnings and are expected to show strong growth over first half 1996, reflecting the full integration of the Provident business.
The Perth-based company plans to double business from sales of life assurance, pensions and investment products over the next three years.
In May, it said it hoped to buy two companies, one dealing in life and the other a general insurance concern with small business expertise though it stressed it would not be rushed into purchases.
